Resolves #19368

`Store.load({append:true})` now admits bulk Pipeline and successful API pages into the held collection. Synchronous commit notifications and the final Pipeline load carry the existing `postChunkLoad` continuation signal, so a bound grid keeps its position. Nonempty parser events suppress a duplicate final aggregate; empty events still permit the final page. Ordinary replacement and caller-owned page selection retain their existing behavior.

Evidence: unit and bound-grid integration coverage meets the close-target contract; no installed UI or deployment effect is claimed. Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `data/StoreApiPipeline.spec.mjs` checks populated Pipeline/API appends, held return values, lazy/eager records and totals. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same spec checks built-in Stream, empty/refused results, emitted-data/final-array admission and ordinary replacement. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: `grid/StoreInteractions.spec.mjs` binds a mounted Grid to the Store and observes actual scroll-reset dispatch; append emits none, replacement does. Store tests check later mutations and sorts do not inherit continuation. |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: both transports' rejected reads retain rows and `currentPage`; explicit `params.page` and its JSDoc pin caller ownership. |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: focused specs and the data/grid regression suites under `playwright.config.unit.mjs`. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. The notification context exists only around synchronous `Store.add`, is restored in `finally`, and does not span the asynchronous read. This extends the owning Store path; consumers need no new handler or event vocabulary. Related: #17835.

Change class: restoration (`fix`). `agent-preflight`: not hosted here; local commit hooks and the shared PR baseline cover the applicable checks.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** two watch items, neither blocking. (1) `postChunkLoad` now means "continuation" for two causes — a streaming chunk and an appended page — under its historical name; both consumers want the same thing today (`grid.Body` suppresses the reset, `list.Buffered` keeps its anchor), but a future consumer reading the name literally could treat an appended page as a stream chunk. A one-line note on the `load` event's doc that the flag means "do not treat this as a fresh data set" would close that reading; a rename is rightly out of scope. (2) Two overlapping appends both commit (no fence, by the ticket's scope); a consumer that fires `load({append})` from a scroll edge still owns its own in-flight gate, as the Institution panes do. I actively looked for a leak of the continuation flag across the asynchronous read and found none: the flag lives only inside `addLoadedItems`' `try`/`finally`, and the "rejected append does not leak continuation" arm pins the post-failure `add` at `false`.
